title: Coherence of normalized etale sum right adjoints
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. All schemes below are Noetherian (admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings), and all arrows are separated and finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Give the arrows and their composites compactifications [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $F_a=Ra_!\dashv G_a$ with counit $\varepsilon_a$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For etale $a$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], put $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})\dashv a^*$ with counit $\operatorname{ev}_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], take $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ from the proper-support/sum identification [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], and define $\rho_a=(d_a^{-1})^c:G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*$ and $\eta_a=\rho_{a,A}$ followed by the pullback-unit identification [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

For composable etale $e:U\to X$ and $v:X\to T$, let $c_{v,e}:G_{ve}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_eG_v$ be the adjunction conjugate of the specified compact-support compositor, using the composite adjunction [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. For every $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\rho_{ve,K}=e^*(\rho_{v,K})\circ\rho_{e,G_vK}\circ c_{v,e,K},$$
with the pullback-composition comparison inserted. For an identity arrow this is the canonical identity comparison.

For a Cartesian base change of an etale $e:U\to X$ along any $w:X'\to X$, write $e':U'\to X'$, $w':U'\to U$ for the pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $C_{e,w}:w^*F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{e'}w'^*$ be the specified compactification exchange [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Define $b_{e,w}:w'^*G_eA_X\to G_{e'}A_{X'}$ as the $F_{e'}\dashv G_{e'}$ adjunct of $w^*\varepsilon_{e,A_X}\circ C_{e,w,G_eA_X}^{-1}$ followed by $w^*A_X\cong A_{X'}$. Then
$$\eta_{e'}\circ b_{e,w}=w'^*\eta_e.$$
The normalizations include the following equality of derived evaluation counits. If $b^\Sigma:w^*S_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{e'}w'^*$ is the inverse of the degreewise sum-extension comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], then, after the pullback identifications,
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,A_X}\circ(b^\Sigma_{e^*A_X})^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',A_{X'}}.$$
These identities use the actual compositor and exchange, agree under proper refinement, and are compatible with further Cartesian open restriction.

source.place: Step 1: identity, composition and arbitrary base-change normalization from sum/evaluation counits

proof.text: Write $L_a=a_{\Sigma!}$ on sheaves and $R_a=a^*$. For an etale $a$, a map from the presheaf $\bigoplus_s M(V,s)$ to a sheaf $N$ is a compatible family $M(V,s)\to N(V)$, hence a map $M\to R_aN$. The sheafification universal property therefore describes the sum adjunction. Its counit sends $i_s(x)$, with $x\in(R_aN)(V,s)=N(V)$, to $x$; it folds finite sums. This is a calculation on the presenting presheaf, not an assertion that all sheaf sections are presheaf sums. Use [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Exactness and the adjunction on the entire unbounded derived categories are supplied by [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]; [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] supplies its termwise counit. Exact inverse image is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so these calculations apply in every degree without boundedness. The localization uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] carries identities of these chain maps to identities of derived natural transformations.

source.place: Tag 03S3 (definition-extension-zero), equation-j-p-shriek and exercise-jshriek-direct; Tag 03S5 (proposition-describe-jshriek); expanded counit calculation

proof.text:
The definition of conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], equivalently the transpose formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], applied to $d_a^{-1}:S_a\to F_a$, says
$$\operatorname{ev}_{a,K}\circ S_a(\rho_{a,K})=\varepsilon_{a,K}\circ d_a^{-1}(G_aK).$$
Equivalently $\varepsilon_{a,K}=\operatorname{ev}_{a,K}\circ S_a(\rho_{a,K})\circ d_a(G_aK)$. Indeed $\rho_{a,K}$ is by definition the $S_a\dashv a^*$ adjunct of the right-hand composite in the first formula, and applying the inverse hom bijection gives the displayed equality. This also proves uniqueness of the right normalization preserving that counit.

source.place: Step 1; elementary expansion of the specified adjunction conjugate

proof.text: For $e,v$ let $\sigma:S_vS_e\to S_{ve}$ denote the derived sum-composition comparison. Its sheaf comparison sends a nested summand labelled by $V\to X$ and $V\to U$ to the summand for the composite lift, as stated in [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact]. Under $(ve)^*\cong e^*v^*$ the counit after this comparison and the composite counit both send each nested generator $i_t(i_s(x))$ to $x$. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], first for the inner and then for the outer sum, proves equality on sheaves. The resulting counit is precisely $\operatorname{ev}_v\circ S_v(\operatorname{ev}_e)$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Thus the conjugate of $\sigma$ is the canonical pullback-composition comparison. This is also clear directly from the two successive hom bijections: both send a family $M(V,s)\to N(V)$ to the same restriction map $M\to e^*v^*N$. Step 1 makes this a degreewise argument on unbounded complexes, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] passes its equality to the derived categories.

source.place: Tags 0F50 (lemma-f-shriek-composition), 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition); etale sum specialization and its explicit counit

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], the actual compact-support compositor $\alpha_{v,e}$ satisfies
$$d_{ve}\circ\alpha_{v,e}=\sigma\circ(d_v S_e)\circ(F_vd_e),$$
where naturality identifies the two possible orders of the middle comparisons. Take conjugates, using compatibility with composition and inverses in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] and pasting along composite adjunctions in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause 2. Step 3 identifies the conjugate of $\sigma$ with the pullback-composition map. Consequently, inserting that map, the resulting equality is exactly
$$\rho_{ve,K}=e^*(\rho_{v,K})\circ\rho_{e,G_vK}\circ c_{v,e,K}.$$
For the identity arrow, $d_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the canonical identity by the identity clause of the same proper-support node; the conjugate of an identity is an identity. The identity adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] therefore gives the asserted identity normalization.

Identify the specified sheaf base-change map before deriving it. Put $H=w^*$, $G=w'^*$, $L=e_{\Sigma!}$, $L'=e'_{\Sigma!}$, $R=e^*$, $R'=e'^*$, and let $\chi:GR\xrightarrow{\sim}R'H$ be the pullback-composition identification. Write $u:\mathrm{id}\to RL$, $v:LR\to\mathrm{id}$ for the sum unit and counit, and $v'$ for the counit of $L'\dashv R'$. The map $\beta:L'G\to HL$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] is characterized by its conjugate $\operatorname{Ex}^0:RH_*\to G_*R'$. The inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions $H\dashv H_*$, $G\dashv G_*$ are [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. If $u^G$ is the latter unit and $v^H$ the former counit, [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] gives
$$\operatorname{Ex}^0_N=G_*(R'(v^H_N)\circ\chi_{H_*N})\circ u^G_{RH_*N}.$$
It is module-linear by [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear]. Consider
$$\widetilde\beta_M=v'_{HL M}\circ L'(\chi_{L M})\circ L'G(u_M).$$
Its transpose across $L'\dashv R'$ is $\chi_{L M}\circ G(u_M)$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Expand its conjugate for $HL\dashv RH_*$ and $L'G\dashv G_*R'$ using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Naturality of $\chi$ moves $R(v_{H_*N})$ next to $u_{RH_*N}$, which cancel by the $L\dashv R$ triangle; the $L'\dashv R'$ triangle has already cancelled in the first transpose. What remains is exactly the displayed formula for $\operatorname{Ex}^0_N$. This is the twofold pasting of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clauses 1 and 2. The conjugate bijection therefore gives $\beta=\widetilde\beta$: the specified $\beta$ is the mate of $\chi$ for the sum adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), proof comparing the two right adjoints; expansion of the two adjunctions

proof.text:
With the notation of Step 5, naturality of $v'$ and $\chi$ gives
$$H(v_N)\circ\beta_{RN}=v'_{HN}\circ L'(\chi_N)\circ L'G(R(v_N)\circ u_{RN})=v'_{HN}\circ L'(\chi_N),$$
since $R(v_N)\circ u_{RN}=1_{RN}$ is the sum-adjunction triangle. Thus the counit square is proved for every sheaf $N$, not just the constant sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], $\beta$ is the specified isomorphism. Apply the equality degreewise to any unbounded representative; Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identify its image with
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ(b^\Sigma_{e^*K})^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',w^*K}\circ S_{e'}(\chi_K).$$
At $K=A_X$, the canonical constant-sheaf identification in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $\chi_{A_X}$ with the identity on $A_{U'}$. This is exactly the required equality of derived evaluation counits.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); counit naturality and the triangle identity on representatives

proof.text:
The proper-support $d_e$ in the statement is, for the chosen compactification $(j,r)$, the comparison $c_e^c$ of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] with its sum identification, which is exactly the comparison normalized in [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility]. Clause (1) of that node, for $g=w$ and the pulled-back compactification $(j',r')$, gives the equality of actual derived transformations
$$(d_{e'}w'^*)\circ C_{e,w}=b^\Sigma\circ(w^*d_e),$$
where its $C^c_{e,w}=Rr'_*(b_j)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_r$ is the proper exchange followed by the inverse open-extension comparison, i.e. the specified exchange of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] on this compactification, and its $b_e$ is our $b^\Sigma$. It applies to any $w$ between Noetherian schemes; no etaleness, flatness or finiteness of $w$ or of $r$ is used. Hence
$$C_{e,w}^{-1}\circ d_{e'}^{-1}=w^*(d_e^{-1})\circ(b^\Sigma)^{-1}.$$
This formula fixes the exchange direction needed when transposing $b_{e,w}$; it uses the pulled-back compactification first, and the same formula for any other chosen one follows from the refinement compatibility in the two cited statements.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); specified proper/open comparison as normalized in the cited nodes

proof.text:
Put $Q=G_eA_X$ and suppress the constant-pullback identifications. By the definition of $b=b_{e,w}$, $\varepsilon_{e',A_{X'}}\circ F_{e'}(b)=w^*\varepsilon_{e,A_X}\circ C_{e,w,Q}^{-1}$. Step 2 and naturality of $d_{e'}$ say that the $S_{e'}\dashv e'^*$ transpose of $\rho_{e',A_{X'}}\circ b$ is
$$w^*\varepsilon_{e,A_X}\circ C_{e,w,Q}^{-1}\circ d_{e'}^{-1}(w'^*Q).$$
Substitute Step 7 and then Step 2. This becomes
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,A_X}\circ w^*S_e(\rho_{e,A_X})\circ(b^\Sigma_Q)^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $(b^\Sigma)^{-1}$ moves $\rho_{e,A_X}$ to the right, giving
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,A_X}\circ(b^\Sigma_{e^*A_X})^{-1}\circ S_{e'}(w'^*\rho_{e,A_X})=\operatorname{ev}_{e',A_{X'}}\circ S_{e'}(\chi_{A_X}\circ w'^*\rho_{e,A_X})$$
by Step 6. The hom bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is injective, so $\rho_{e',A_{X'}}\circ b=\chi_{A_X}\circ w'^*\rho_{e,A_X}$. Compose with $e'^*A_{X'}\cong A_{U'}$; the constant identifications of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identify the right side with $w'^*\eta_e$. This proves $\eta_{e'}\circ b_{e,w}=w'^*\eta_e$.

source.place: Step 1: base-change normalization; explicit equality of the two counit transposes

proof.text: Finally take a proper refinement or a further Cartesian restriction by an open immersion. The $d_a$ comparisons agree under proper refinement by [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact]; the actual $\alpha$ and $C$ agree by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and the base-change square of Step 7 agrees with the proper-refinement identifications by the last sentence of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility]. Consequently their defining left-adjoint equalities, and hence their unique right-adjoint transposes, are unchanged. For successive base changes the pullback-composition maps $\chi$ paste by associativity of inverse image; the mates $\beta$ paste by clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. The compact-support exchanges paste by the cited unbounded-comparisons statement. Applying the transpose calculation of Step 8 to the pasted square therefore gives the composite of its calculations for the two squares. An open restriction is such a base change, so the displayed identities commute with every further Cartesian open restriction. No choice of a new right-adjoint normalization is made.
